newsitem.title: USA: Earth First! leader Judi Bari dies in California.
newsitem.headline: Earth First! leader Judi Bari dies in California.

text.p: Environmental activist Judi Bari, who received international attention after she was injured in a 1990 car bombing, died in California on Sunday of cancer, her attorney said. She was 47.

A leader of the environmental group Earth First!, Bari was seriously injured in the Oakland, Calif., car explosion, which also hurt a fellow activist. Bari at the time was involved in organising protests against logging in northern California redwood forests.

Oakland police arrested Bari in the bombing. They suspected she was carrying the explosives to use in a terrorist attack, but no charges were filed against her, Bari's attorney, Dennis Cunningham, said.

Bari later sued the Oakland police and the FBI, alleging they tried to portray her as a suspect in order to smear Earth First!. She also alleged they failed to investigate the bombing and destroyed evidence, her attorney said.
Bari died at about 6:45 A.M. local time at her home just outside Willits, about 120 miles (190 km) north of San Francisco. She was suffering from breast cancer that had spread to her liver.
"She'll be sorely missed," said Gary Ball, a fellow Earth First! activist. "But I think her passing will be cause for doubling and redoubling our determination and effort."
She is survived by her parents, two sisters and two daughters, Cunningham said.
He added that Bari's lawsuit against the Oakland police and the FBI would still be pursued after her death.
